samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (pañcamī: the source in the ablative; उत्थ from उद् + √स्था with the suffix -a, feminine -ā)

morph.note: Feminine in -ī of भ्रामर (11.53): ‘she of the bees’. The name is taken from the form, as Raktadantikā and Śatākṣī were.
उत्था: उद् + √स्था, the s of स्था lost after उद् (उत्था-), with the agent suffix -a: ‘that which rises up’.

mantras.anvaya: तदा च लोकाः सर्वतः मां ‘भ्रामरी’ इति स्तोष्यन्ति। इत्थं यदा यदा दानवोत्था बाधा भविष्यति, (11.55: तदा तदा …)
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line closes the fifth descent with the name; the second begins the closing generalisation, a distributive यदा यदा-clause whose correlative तदा तदा is in 11.55.
mantras.lit: And then the people everywhere will praise me as ‘Bhrāmarī’. Thus, whenever affliction arising from the Dānavas shall occur, —
mantras.tr: and people everywhere will then praise me as Bhrāmarī. Thus, whenever oppression born of the demons arises,
mantras.tr_note: ‘Demons’ renders दानव (the sons of Danu); the sentence is completed in 11.55.

comm.t: The fifth form is named: Bhrāmarī, ‘she of the bees’, praised everywhere. With इत्थम्, ‘thus’, the Goddess turns from the list of named descents to a rule: whenever demons cause affliction.

After the daughter of Yaśodā (11.42) the prophecy has named six forms in four descents: Raktadantikā; Śatākṣī, Śākambharī and Durgā (one descent, 11.46–50); Bhīmā; and Bhrāmarī. The Mūrtirahasya recited after the Saptaśatī gives meditations on these forms.

words.g: indeclinable; repeated for distribution, answering यदा यदा: ‘each time then’
first-person pronoun अस्मद्, nom. sg.; subject
m. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); object of करिष्यामि

sandhi.note: ā + a → ā twice: तदा + अवतीर्य → तदावतीर्य, अवतीर्य + अहम् → अवतीर्याहम्. The m becomes anusvāra before k (8.3.23).
i before the unlike vowel a becomes y.

samasa.sense: the ending of the foes (of the worlds and the gods)

morph.note: Repetition for distribution (vīpsā): यदा यदा … तदा तदा ‘whenever … each time then’. The doubled word makes a single promise into a standing rule.
Future of √कृ with iṭ (कर् + इष्य + आमि). With अरिसंक्षयम्, ‘I shall make an end of the enemies’ — the last verb of the chapter.

mantras.anvaya: (यदा यदा दानवोत्था बाधा भविष्यति,) तदा तदा अहम् अवतीर्य अरिसंक्षयं करिष्यामि॥
mantras.anvaya_en: The correlative clause of 11.54b: the doubled तदा तदा, the absolutive अवतीर्य, the verb करिष्यामि and its object.
mantras.lit: — then, each time, having descended, I shall bring about the destruction of the enemies.
mantras.tr: each time I shall descend and destroy the enemies.
mantras.tr_note: The half-śloka completes the sentence begun in 11.54; ‘each time’ renders the doubled तदा.

comm.t: The prophecy closes in a rule: whenever demons afflict the worlds, the Goddess will descend (अवतीर्य) and destroy the enemies. This answers the gods’ request of 11.39 exactly: एवम् एव, ‘in just this way’, every time. A half-śloka, counted by the Gita Press as its own mantra; the closing ॐ belongs to the recitation.

The construction recalls the Bhagavadgītā’s promise of descent (4.7–8, यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य …): the same यदा यदा and the same idea of a recurring descent. Here the one who descends is the Goddess, and the occasion is the oppression of the worlds by demons.
A modern reading: the chapter ends not with a final victory but with a promise of return. The text treats protection as a pattern that repeats, not a single event.
